juce::FileOutputStream Class Reference

## Detailed Description

An output stream that writes into a local file.

See also[OutputStream](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1OutputStream.html "The base class for streams that write data to some kind of destination."), [FileInputStream](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1FileInputStream.html "An input stream that reads from a local file."), [File::createOutputStream](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1File.html#a01664377d2c267dc69564534985923f5 "Creates a stream to write to this file.")

Creates a [FileOutputStream](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1FileOutputStream.html "An output stream that writes into a local file.").

If the file doesn't exist, it will first be created. If the file can't be created or opened (for example, because the parent directory of the file does not exist), the [failedToOpen()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1FileOutputStream.html#a789365070cf21efb131652b11ee90ef3 "Returns true if the stream couldn't be opened for some reason.") method will return true.

If the file already exists when opened, the stream's write-position will be set to the end of the file. To overwrite an existing file, you can truncate it like this:

```cpp
FileOutputStream stream (file);

if (stream.openedOk())
{
    stream.setPosition (0);
    stream.truncate();
    ...
}
```

Destroying a [FileOutputStream](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1FileOutputStream.html "An output stream that writes into a local file.") object does not force the operating system to write the buffered data to disk immediately. If this is required you should call [flush()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1FileOutputStream.html#ad947b281d8eeada57303809615e4c5ee "If the stream is using a buffer, this will ensure it gets written out to the destination.") before triggering the destructor.

See also[TemporaryFile](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1TemporaryFile.html "Manages a temporary file, which will be deleted when this object is deleted.")

◆ FileOutputStream()

juce::FileOutputStream::FileOutputStream ( const File & fileToWriteTo,
size_t bufferSizeToUse = 16384 )

Creates a FileOutputStream.

If the file doesn't exist, it will first be created. If the file can't be created or opened (for example, because the parent directory of the file does not exist), the failedToOpen() method will return true.

If the file already exists when opened, the stream's write-position will be set to the end of the file. To overwrite an existing file, you can truncate it like this:

FileOutputStream stream (file);
 
if (stream.openedOk())
{
    stream.setPosition (0);
    stream.truncate();
    ...
}

Destroying a FileOutputStream object does not force the operating system to write the buffered data to disk immediately. If this is required you should call flush() before triggering the destructor.
